raw_text:
- The objective of this research is to investigate why repeated responses to the same question can differ and to identify the observable factors responsible for such variation.

Assumptions
- Respondents provide honest and sincere responses.
- The difference in responses is not solely due to random chance.

Research design
- Quasi-experimental design will be employed to observe and compare responses to the same question among different groups.

Data or evidence needed
- High-frequency responses from a diverse population to the same question over a specified period.
- Observations on contextual factors during response attempts (e.g., stress level, time pressure).

Measurement
- Frequency and consistency of responses.
- Use of standardized questionnaires to ensure uniformity.
- Contextual factors measured through surveys or direct observation.

Analysis
- Descriptive statistics to summarize response data. 
- Inferential statistics to identify relationships between variables (contextual factors and response consistency).
- Hierarchical linear modeling (HLM) to account for potential nesting within groups.

Decision / stopping rule
- Collect data from a predetermined sample size (n = 200). 
- Continue data collection until convergence in the patterns of response consistency among groups is observed.

Limitations
- Self-report biases in contextual factor measurements.
- External factors (e.g., changes in the environment) could influence response consistency across time.
